recipes.name: Mama’s Squash Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 sleeve buttery round crackers (such as Ritz®), crushed, divided
2 cups shredded sharp Cheddar cheese, divided

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 1-quart casserole dish.

Place a steamer insert into a saucepan and fill with water to just below the bottom of the steamer. Bring water to a boil. Add squash and onion, cover, and steam until squash is tender and easily mashed with a fork, 10 to 15 minutes.
Whisk egg and sour cream together in the prepared casserole dish; add squash, onions, 2/3 of the crackers, and 2/3 of the Cheddar cheese. Stir with a fork.
Cover the squash mixture with remaining Cheddar cheese and crackers.
Bake in the preheated oven until hot and bubbly and topping is golden brown, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Mama’s Squash Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This cheesy squash casserole recipe is quick and easy to prepare and bake with a buttery cracker topping for a family-approved comforting side dish.

review.reviewBody: I had only 3 summer squash to use up so I halved the recipe. But I still used an entire onion, which I carmelized in olive oil instead of steaming. I highly recommend carmelizing the onion and also leaving the squash al dente instead of mushy. I also used the whole egg. I didn't have a "sleeve" of Ritz crackers so I had to estimate with club crackers. Since I had used a whole egg, I used enough cracker crumbs to make the whole thing come together. I also used Cheddar cheese with black pepper which made the whole thing spicier. I really enjoyed this recipe and will make again. Thanks!

Superb. Used homemade sourdough croutons and cornbread stuffing mix instead of crackers. Used softened cream cheese instead of sour cream, as that was on hand. Added a bit of sea salt and a dash of iodized salt to the squash mixture. Added ground pepper on top of the shredded cheese top layer before covering with the cornbread stuffing.

What do you do with all your summer squash? This is the question. Well here's your answer. This recipe is so good! 
 I did caramelize the onions as other posters suggested. I added 1,garlic clove (because we love garlic), then sautéd the squash for a brief time instead of steaming. Mixed it all together and BAM! Deliciousness! Hubby raved about it. Oh yeah the new squash recipe. I am going to try zuchinni next.

I used half summer squash and half zucchini, and I also sautéed the onion and squashes instead of steaming them based on the recommendation of others. I added a clove of garlic because I love it. I was able to smash the veggies with the edge of a wooden spatula once they were soft. It was yummy, and I’ll make it again for sure. I also only added the crushed crackers to the top as a personal preference.

This was a hit in my house. I didn't add the crackers. We are diabetic and don't use much crackers and bread crumbs. I cooked the onions and squash in a pan with a lid. Added salt and pepper. And used Hooped Cheese. Yummy. Will make it again.

Ok.. I’m a horrible cook, I’m not ganna sugar coat it but, I did make this and it came out well! I cheated by pan cooking/frying the onion and squash in 2 tank spoons if butter while I whisked the sour cream and egg together in a separate bowl. I only used 4 yellow squash and 3/4 of an onion. I didn’t have crackers so I used bread crumbs. I should have drained the onion and squash before incorporating into the sour cream mixture. I added bread crumbs and cheese to dry it up but kept it moist. Poured it into a 8x11 greased pan and sprinkled remaining cheese and shook some bread crumbs over the top (about 1/2 cup) and popped in oven for about 45 minutes. I would definitely make this again.
Great recipe. I have already made it twice. I carmelized the onions in olive oil and cookid the squash with it. I did not smash the squash. I substituted panko for crackers.

Loved this recipe! I cut it in half and used 3 larger sized squash. I did as others suggested and caramelized my onion and sautéed the sliced squash. I didn't add any salt or pepper to the sour cream and egg mixture but will for sure next time. I will add more cheese also. I thought this turned out really good but my husband just thought it was so-so and needed more flavor. I am excited that I get to have all the left-overs to myself! Thank you for an awesome recipe it will be made often during the summer while my garden is producing! YUM!

I scaled this down a bit as only 2 of us...I ended up using zucchini as I had plenty on hand. I sauteed the onions and added 1 clove of fresh garlic to the onions at the end of cooking. I only had club crackers as well...all in all a very yummy dish made this way, - thanks for the inspiration to enjoy my squash!

This was fabulous and just like I remember it from growing up in the south. I only did one thing differently. I sauted the squash and onions in butter and a bit of olive oil rather than steam and it turned out so good! This is a keeper!

I added1/2 can unsalted corn and 2 7oz cans green chili. Seasoned with s&p, garlic powder, and smoked paprika, greased dish with both coconut lard and real butter. I also used green Mexican summer squash, 6, that were free- capped and ended, cut in half length wise and salted for 3 hours (to extract much of the liquid) before rinsed and sliced. I used El Mexican Savadorian Creme. I would cut back the crackers to 1/3 sleeve. This was good. I would make it again
Needs seasoning. Also, better 2nd time because i carmel7zed the onions
Really great recipe! I usually add extra seasoning and add some ricotta in as well for extra flavor and richness!
I personally would use a cup and a half of sour cream next time, maybe add a tablespoon of butter.

Great way to use up some squash. My family (including my son) loved it! Only change I made was using some crispy onions on the top instead of the crackers. I still included crackers in the squash mix, though.
Just for me so I tried to make it 1/2.....too dry for my liking...plus in the beginning it states cook time 40 minutes...and then at the bottom it says in oven for 30 minutes...so which is it?
It is good but I am adding more sour cream and Italian seasoning this time for more flavor . I only added half of the sour cream last time.
Was not a fan in my household.
I made it this evening and was super disappointed. It was lacking in flavor for sure. Next time, I am going to try to sautee the squash and onions and add garlic, salt, thyme and onion powder.
